goal: FIRST INTEGRATION, under the overall vision. Make the Minecraft engine feed Jev (the in-game decision maker) a coherent, category-structured picture of its world and the whole supported possibility space, so Jev chooses and the engine executes through shared, parameter-driven mechanics and confirms the real effect. Governing instruction: the owner's product instruction for the Minecraft engine, kept outside this repository; it replaces only the descriptions it contradicts, not earlier valid technical requirements. Survival is only the current physical frame and one possible test, never the product goal and never a hidden ladder. The engine must not make new strategic choices: a nearby threat, damage or an unsure model answer must not silently remove options or end a session as a policy. The engine does keep its mechanical role: performing the execution Jev chose, technical validity checks, stop and disconnect handling, and carrying out conditional plans Jev has already chosen. First coherent delivery: the whole chain shown once end to end - fresh facts, several real and comparable possibilities, Jev's own choice, shared execution, confirmed effect in the game, and the next choice from the confirmed state. A passed loop completes this stage. Later stages stay required and are recorded here as follow-on work, not dropped: LLM knowledge intake and reuse; composing new possibilities out of the available mechanics; situation-dependent development of goals; building, rebuilding and preservation. Earlier valid technical requirements remain: measured budgets instead of constants tuned to one user's latency, no wait-only stalling, and honest reporting of what could not be confirmed. Creative is an early practice and test environment for world understanding, building, digging, renovation and preservation: it complements this instruction rather than replacing it, and survival is exercised from the beginning so abilities and plans are also checked under the real constraints. Creative and survival share one engine - the same world model, decision path, plan format and shared mechanics - with the game mode and the actual abilities visible to Jev, and with execution differing only where the game's rules force it. A plan that worked with flight and unlimited materials is not thereby verified in survival. Creative testing is a method, not a required order for the bot's ordinary gameplay, and nothing waits for a finished creative bot before survival is examined. The practice environment is the dedicated Multiverse world minecraft:dt (creative, peaceful, flight allowed), verified to be fully isolated from the operator's survival world; survival is therefore checked in the survival world, and neither environment's result is reported as the other's.
acceptance: A short chain-status document (docs/chain-status.md) exists that states, from the current code and the current recordings, exactly what Jev receives, which choices it is offered, which of them the engine can execute, and where the chain breaks. It must not quote an older plan as if it were current behaviour, and it must name the governing instruction.

One governing contract is documented and enforced by tests: every offered possibility carries a unique meaning with concrete parameters, its known prerequisites with visible uncertainty, its execution status (implemented / partially implemented / known but not supported), an observable success criterion including the partial result, and a way to cancel or fail with a stated reason.

Missing implementation and missing prerequisites in the world are kept apart. An action the engine cannot perform is never offered as choosable; instead the possibility of investigation, learning, planning and acquiring the prerequisites for a future goal stays on the menu as long as the engine can really support it. A test fails if an offered id lacks an executor without being marked knowledge-only, or if a supported investigative or planning option is withheld from the menu.

The engine makes no new strategic choice: an enemy in range and lost health do not remove the productive possibilities and do not end the session as a policy; staying put or continuing current work is offered as a real option again. The engine keeps its mechanical duties - executing what Jev chose, technical validity checks, stop and disconnect handling, running conditional plans Jev already chose - and any remaining automatic reaction is narrowly scoped, documented and recorded as a fallback rather than a hidden policy.

The same shared execution path handles at least two materials with different prerequisites and drops (wood and a stone-class material), proven through the same harvest/placement/craft mechanics rather than a scene-specific script, with tests over both.

Live evidence of the whole chain in the operator's own server and Java test world: one bounded run where Jev receives several real alternatives, chooses, the engine executes through the shared path, and the effect is confirmed by an independent readback (inventory and block reads) saved with the recording and its hash. A fixture, an adapter acknowledgement or a process exit is not this evidence.

The whole decision chain is measured and reported as p50/p95/p99 with the data sizes and test conditions - observation, world-model update, lookup, request build, model answer, dispatch, observed effect - and the world index is used in that real path, not only in an isolated test. It is not enough that the index alone is fast.
An independent review checks the acceptance criteria and the gameplay evidence, not only that the configured checks are green, and its verdict is recorded unchanged.

This run is the first integration under the overall vision. The later stages named in the goal - LLM knowledge intake and reuse, composing new possibilities, situation-dependent goal development, and building, rebuilding and preservation - are not acceptance criteria of this stage, but they must not be contradicted or closed off by what this stage builds.

Game mode and actual abilities are part of what Jev receives: the observation states whether the bot is in survival or creative (and any other mode the server sets) and what that changes about the offered possibilities, so the same plan can be judged under either set of rules. A test fails if the mode is missing or is silently inferred from an assumption.

The same plan format and decision path serve both modes: at least one small representative project is verified first in creative and then executed in survival under calm, known conditions, with any starting materials stated, and anything that only works because of creative's flight or unlimited materials is marked as not verified in survival rather than reported as working.

Recorded experience carries its conditions: what was tried, what worked or failed, the game mode and the necessary prerequisites are stored with the recording, and no plan is reported as survival-verified unless a survival run itself confirmed the effect.

Creative is where the ability set is developed before survival has to carry it: spatial understanding, adaptable build plans, placement, removal, replacement and preservation of functions that must keep working. The same plan stays revisable by Jev while it runs, and a Jev Router LLM may add knowledge or a plan proposal, which the engine then offers as possibilities rather than executing on its own. At least one such ability is shown through the shared mechanics by tests, and the same plan is then shown in survival under stated conditions.

Learning is kept as durable, checkable knowledge rather than as narration: the engine can hand Jev what was already tried, under which mode and prerequisites, and whether it worked, and that record is reused when a similar situation returns instead of being rediscovered. A test fails if a recorded experience cannot be read back and attached to the situation it belongs to.

Every reported ability names the world and the game mode that confirmed it, and anything practised only in minecraft:dt is marked as not yet verified in survival until a survival run confirms the same plan. A session must never be counted as surviving merely because it worked where flight and unlimited materials were available.

build.when: Implementation, contract or world-description code is missing or incomplete relative to the goal
build.brief: Implement one coherent slice of the engine: the world description, the possibility catalogue, the shared mechanics, or the wiring between them. Keep the product vision in the instruction; do not add a hidden strategic filter and do not encode a fixed survival ladder. Keep the engine's mechanical duties (execution, validity checks, stop/disconnect, chosen conditional plans) and put every new strategic choice through Jev's decision path. Write implementation and documentation, never tests. Do not run the configured checks; the loop server runs them.

test.when: Tests are missing or do not cover an acceptance criterion
test.brief: Write tests that verify the acceptance criteria, including the contract fields of every offered possibility, the split between missing implementation and missing prerequisites, the removal of engine-side strategic vetoes, and the shared execution path over two materials. Do not change implementation code. Do not run the configured checks; the loop server runs them.

fix.when: Checks or review fail with concrete errors or gaps
fix.brief: Read the check or review evidence and fix the root cause with the smallest correct change. If a gap is missing gameplay evidence, produce that evidence rather than a description of it. Never weaken an acceptance criterion to make a check pass. Do not run the configured checks; the loop server runs them.

verify.when: The chain must be shown in the real game rather than only in tests
verify.brief: Run one bounded live session against the operator's own Java test world through the documented local connection, record it, and read the effect back independently (inventory, block and dimension reads). Never change server rules, world configuration or gamerules, never print credentials, and state every operator action that touched the server. Report what was observed, including a failure to confirm. Creative mode may be used for the practice run, and the same plan must then be shown in survival under stated conditions; report which mode produced which observation, and never present a creative result as survival evidence.
